t:
No part of any appropriation contained in this title shall be used for construction of any ship in any foreign country.
This title may be cited as the “Department of Commerce Appropriation Act, 1969”.

fable.w: This section only restricts how appropriated funds may be spent (no ship construction in a foreign country) and supplies a short title. No outside party is consulted, heard, appointed to a body, or given a right to sue over any federal decision, so there is no participation; the reference to a foreign country is merely a location for the spending limit.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this title shall be used for construction of any ship in any foreign country.

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a restriction on the use of federal funds (appropriations) for ship construction. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_block.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this title shall be used for construction of any ship in any foreign country.

opus.w: This provision only limits how appropriated funds may be used and gives the Act its short title. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this title shall be used for construction of any ship in any foreign country.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a restriction on the use of federal funds, prohibiting the construction of ships in foreign countries. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as foreign governments, companies, or the public) in making this decision. The text is purely a statutory limitation on appropriations.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this title shall be used for construction of any ship in any foreign country.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the prohibition on foreign construction implies a decision-making process involving foreign entities, but the text itself contains no mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside party. It is a simple funding restriction.
